findings.result_name: v14:prop-fv-stall (the few-denominator class does contain stalls)
findings.defect: The proposition is stated "For n >= 3" and marked PROVED, but its proof is a schema that reduces to three n-dependent finite exact checks (F(W) >= W, Theta >= Psi/2, D_K >= W + t*Psi at K=14), and the route's own proof text carries them out only for n = 3, 4, 5. The universal quantifier over n is unproved. GAP (one self-contained sentence): for every n >= 3, with F one round of the mechanism on FV(n) or FV_2(n), W(x,y) = w*(x)-w*(y), D_14 the 14th iterate from D_0 = 1, S = {(x,y) : D_14(x,y) > W(x,y)}, Psi = 1_S and Theta the c-derivative of F(W + c*Psi) at 0+, one has Theta >= Psi/2 and D_14 >= W + min(min_S(D_14 - W), 1/(12N))*Psi.
findings.evidence: verify14.tex line 532ff: statement "For $n\ge3$ ...", proof ends "The three checks were carried out in exact arithmetic for $n=3,4,5$ and both variants." I rebuilt the checks myself (/tmp/.../audit-verify-r14-correctness/fvproofcheck.py, .out) and they DO pass at K=14 for n=3..8, both FV and FV_2, both M2 and M2T (check1 F(W)==W, linearity of F(W+cPsi) confirmed at two values of c, check2, check3, own-successor entries in S all True), and correctly fail the own-in-S clause at n=2 where the rule fires at round 4. So the statement is now verified for 3 <= n <= 8 — still not proved for all n. The proof's analytic core is sound: I re-derived the breakpoint bound (W-combinations are multiples of 1/6; Psi-coefficients after one slack step + min-plus closure lie in [0,N] and are multiples of 1/2, so no breakpoint lies in (0,1/(6N))), F(W)=W exactly, and the induction D_{K+j} >= W + t*2^{-j}*Psi.

findings.result_name: v14:prop-fv-stall / v14:rem-fewden — the headline "item (6) is answered in the NEGATIVE"
findings.defect: The open item (rem:alphabet-compare) asks whether {D <= poly} contains a stall for any of M1-M6 OR def:bsi. The route addresses M2, M2T, M4, M1 and M5 only; M6 (the ratio calculus) and def:bsi are untouched, and on FV(n) BSI is trivially non-stalling. Moreover the exhibited "stall" is one that def:decision-rule explicitly licenses: a rule may abstain exactly when every controlled vertex has equal-valued successors, which is the case on all of FV(n)/FV_2(n) — and prop:fv-family already says in the paper that these families "show nothing about the frontier". The proposition's title, "The few-denominator class does contain stalls", therefore asserts more than is shown, even though the following remark honestly labels the stalls vacuous and states the real gap.
findings.evidence: On FV(3) and FV(4) I verified by exhaustive computation that EVERY Max strategy and EVERY Min strategy is optimal (val_sigma == val^tau == w* for all 2^n of each), so S_sigma = S^tau = empty at every pair and def:bsi halts at round 0 from any start. M4's own-successor separators are identically 0 (fvm4b.py, n=3,4,5, both families) — as they must be, since Sep(v^(i),v) >= w*(v)-w*(v^(i)) = 0 and <= 0 by the Max row; no computation is needed and the "M4 stall" is a one-line consequence of rem:own-successor. The M1 and M5 contrast claims DO check out: the value-simulation preorder decides every controlled vertex on FV(n)/FV_2(n) for n=3,4,5 (fvm14.py), and the full def:hybrid decides every controlled vertex at round 2 on FV(3) and round 3 on FV_2(3) (fvm5c.out).

findings.defect: The final clause "while the switch from q to p is endorsed whenever it is improving" is stated for both variants but is FALSE for the strict variant: the strict Max veto is U(p) > U(q), which by the lemma's own first sentence fails exactly when val^tau(a) = val^tau(b). The proof only establishes the non-strict form ("the veto for q->p reads val^tau(p) >= val^tau(q), which always holds").
findings.evidence: Explicit 6-vertex stopping counterexample (audit .../bias.py): kinds (max,max,avg,avg,min,avg), succ (1,2),(3,4),(3,4),(t1,t0),(5,3),(t0,t0); v=0, p=1, q=2, a=3, b=4. With sigma = (v->q, p->a) and tau(b)=a: val_sigma(p)=1/2 > val_sigma(q)=1/4 so q->p is improving, yet val^tau(p)=val^tau(q)=1/2, so the strict variant does not endorse it. The non-strict variant does. Everything else in the lemma is correct (max dominates mean, equality iff the arguments agree), and the ladder application is unaffected.

findings.evidence: q16count.py: internal-node counts of the collapsed depth-6 trees, per leaf order. Vertex-index order 270 (N=288); t0-first index order 271; decreasing mass 277 (N=295) and 277 under every tie-break; best of 4000 random target orders 263 (N=281). Exhaustive min/max over ALL target permutations for all 32 actions: minimum 227 average vertices (N = 245), maximum 396 (N = 414). So 240 (N=258) is attainable by some order and "at most 258" is true; in fact "at most 245" is provable, and 238 is attainable by some order but not by decreasing mass. A lower bound of 221 (N = 239) follows from sum-of-popcounts.

findings.defect: The paste-ready LaTeX describes the algorithm as "iterates T-hat two-sidedly ... doubling p through 2,4,8,... and restarting, stopping when the width falls below 4^{-a}" but never says WHEN to restart. At a precision p below the stated threshold the width converges to roughly kappa-hat*2^{1-p}/(1-lambda-hat) > 4^{-a} and never falls below it, so the loop as written does not terminate. The route's report states the missing budget ("2^s rounds at p = 2^s") but the LaTeX does not.
findings.evidence: verify14.tex lines 441-491. The width bound the proof derives, ||d_k||_inf <= kappa-hat*lambda-hat^k + kappa-hat*2^{1-p}/(1-lambda-hat), has a p-dependent floor; I re-derived it (d_{k+1} <= S-hat d_k + 2^{1-p}*1 from directed rounding, then the x-hat-weighted norm) and confirm both terms and the two threshold computations. The kappa-hat repair the route identifies is necessary and correct; only the termination clause is missing from the statement.

findings.defect: The results field says "Delta_k(X_0,L_0) = 2^{-floor((k-1)/2)} on FV(3), still 1/549755813888 at k=60". The formula is the plain slack calculus M2 (which gives 1/536870912 = 2^{-29} at k=60); 1/549755813888 = 2^{-39} is the M2T (min-plus closed) value. The paste-ready remark v14:rem-fewden prints only the formula, so the deliverable is consistent; the report is not.

The (<=) direction says "the certificate x = (I - A_pi)^{-1} 1 of thm:prec-rate(ii)" for a single profile pi. A certificate must satisfy S x <= lambda x for S = max over ALL profiles; a single-profile resolvent gives only M_pi x <= lambda x for that pi. The step is repaired by taking x to be the nonlinear resolvent, the fixed point of x = 1 + S x / lambda, and letting pi be its argmax policy — then x = (I - A_pi)^{-1} 1 holds for that pi and the Cramer/Hadamard bound applies verbatim. As written the step is asserted and rests on thm:prec-rate(ii), which is outside the supplied material.
findings.evidence: The rest of the proof is correct and I checked it: lambda = 1 - 1/(3p) gives lambda^2 >= 1 - 2/(3p) >= 1 - 1/p >= Lambda, hence rho(A_pi) = rho(M_pi)/lambda <= lambda < 1; |det(I - A_pi)| >= (1-lambda)^n and Hadamard on the cofactors give log_2 ||x||_inf = O(n log n + n log(3p)), polynomial; and kappa(x) <= ||x||_inf since min x >= 1. The engine equivalence the route tested (a certificate at rate lambda exists iff rho(M_pi) < lambda for every profile) I retested independently on 120 random stopping SSGs x 3 random rational rates = 360 exact tests, LP feasibility against the exact M-matrix criterion: 0 mismatches (esceq.py).

findings.evidence: las2two.py / las2diag.py: 40 random |C| = 2 stopping SSGs on 8 non-sinks; for every point of a 25x25 rational grid lying in Q~(G) I solved the two complementarity equalities over the 2x2 PSD cone exactly (affine slice of the Lorentz cone, quadratic feasibility in closed form). On average 55 grid points lie in Q~; in every game exactly one is feasible, namely w*|_C (which is feasible in all 40 by construction, with S = 0). No feasible u different from w*|_C anywhere.
